page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-hypermem-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine provisioned within the Network Optimized server family. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 62.0 GB of system memory, it provides an elevated memory-to-core ratio of 15.5 GB per virtual CPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, leaving disk operations reliant on remote persistent block storage options.

The hardware configuration provides high memory density relative to its compute footprint, avoiding CPU over-provisioning when processing large in-memory working sets. Because local storage is absent and network interfaces supply data persistence, total I/O throughput is coupled with external storage network performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM allocation per core benefits applications constrained by memory footprint rather than raw computational cycles. This makes the machine suitable for in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, and data processing pipelines requiring substantial memory headroom per worker thread.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4n-hypermem-4 is an x86_64 instance within the Network Optimized family, featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs paired with 62.0 GB of system RAM. This delivers a substantial 15.5 GB of memory per core, making it suitable for applications with heavy working memory demands relative to processing power. The server includes no local SSD storage and zero GPU accelerators, operating entirely with detached network-attached storage solutions. Due to its memory density, the instance offers cost-efficient scaling for workloads that require significant memory footprints without paying for unneeded CPU cores. Primary use cases include in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, memory-bound ETL batch jobs, and analytics workloads requiring high data retention in memory.
